question: How can a fully open dense LM family (7B, 13B, 32B) be trained stably and compute-efficiently, and which pretraining, mid-training (annealing) and post-training choices produce competitive base and instruct models?
hypothesis: Architecture and initialisation changes remove loss and gradient-norm spikes, and a late-stage curriculum on high-quality and synthetic math data, with checkpoint averaging, gives large gains per FLOP (a higher learning rate during pretraining is conjectured to make annealing more effective).
contributions: OLMo 2 7B, 13B and 32B base models with weights, data, code, recipes, logs and intermediate checkpoints released
Pretraining stability interventions (repeated n-gram filter, init, RMSNorm, reordered norm, QK-norm, z-loss, AdamW epsilon, no weight decay on embeddings)
Mid-training recipe: Dolmino Mix 1124, microanneals for assessing data sources, checkpoint souping
OLMo 2-Instruct via the Tulu 3 recipe with permissive data and multi-stage RLVR
Infrastructure notes and energy, carbon and water accounting

method.summary: Decoder-only transformers (7B/13B/32B, plus a 1B used for experiments) are pretrained in two stages: stage 1 on OLMo 2 Mix 1124 (about 3.9T tokens, over 95% web) with cosine LR, then stage 2 mid-training on Dolmino Mix 1124 with linear LR decay to zero, repeated with different data orders and averaged (souping). Post-training follows Tulu 3 (SFT, DPO with on-policy preferences, RLVR).

datasets.name: OLMo 2 Mix 1124
datasets.source: DCLM-Baseline 3.71T tokens; StarCoder filtered 83.0B; peS2o 58.6B; arXiv 20.8B; OpenWebMath 12.2B; Algebraic Stack 11.8B; Wikipedia & Wikibooks 3.7B
datasets.preprocessing: StarCoder: drop docs from repos with fewer than 2 stars, docs whose most frequent word is over 30% or top-2 words over 50%; all documents with 32 or more repeated n-grams (n = 1 to 13 tokens) removed

datasets.name: Dolmino Mix 1124 (source pool)
datasets.size: High quality subset 832.6B tokens; math mix 10.7B tokens; sampled into 50B, 100B and 300B token mixes
datasets.source: DCLM FastText top 7% + FineWeb-Edu >=2 web 752B; decontaminated FLAN 17.0B; peS2o 58.6B; Wikipedia 3.7B; StackExchange Q&A 1.26B; math: TuluMath 230M, DolminoSynthMath 28.7M, TinyGSM-MIND 6.48B, MathCoder2 synthetic 3.87B, Metamath OWM-filtered 84.2M, CodeSearchNet OWM-filtered 1.78M, GSM8K train 2.74M
datasets.preprocessing: FLAN dropped where 10% or more n-gram overlap with any eval instance; StackExchange kept questions with accepted answer, 3+ question votes, 5+ answer votes; DCLM fastText threshold 0.033110 retains about 65.6% of web, FineWeb-Edu score >=3 keeps 5.8%, >=2 keeps 20.3%; math from GPT-4o persona-driven generation, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct MIND rewrites, FastText math classifier trained on 10,000 GPT-4o-labelled OpenWebMath docs

datasets.name: Dolmino 50B / 100B / 300B mixes
datasets.source: Table 13: in the 50B mix filtered DCLM 47.2%, FLAN 16.6%, StackExchange 2.45%, peS2o 5.85%, Wikipedia 7.11%, Math 20.8%; DCLM about 50% in all mixes
datasets.preprocessing: StackExchange and math repeated 2x for 100B and 4x for 300B; FLAN 2x and Wiki 4x for 300B

datasets.name: OLMES base eval suite

datasets.name: DPO preference data

models.name: OLMo 2 7B
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, MHA, SwiGLU, RoPE theta 5e5, RMSNorm, reordered norm, QK-norm, z-loss
models.tokenizer: cl100k-derived pre-tokenizer and vocab plus PII masking tokens

models.name: Qwen 2.5, Gemma 2/3, Mistral, DCLM 7B, Amber, MAP Neo, StableLM 2, Zamba 2, SmolLM2, OLMo-0424

training.objective: next-token cross-entropy plus z-loss 1e-4 * log2(Z)^2 (text prints 10^-4 * log2 Z; Table 1 lists z-loss weight 10^-5)
training.lr_schedule: stage 1: cosine decay to 10% of peak over 5T tokens (7B, 13B) or 6.5T (32B); 7B truncated after 4T, 32B after 6T; stage 2: linear decay to zero
training.tokens: 7B 4.05T total (3.90T pretraining); 13B 5.6T (5T pretraining); 32B 6.6T (6.06T pretraining); mid-training 7B: 3 x 50B; 13B and 32B: 3 x 100B + 1 x 300B
training.weight_decay: 0.1 (update multiplies each parameter by 1 - 0.1*lr); embeddings excluded
training.regularisation: z-loss; no weight decay on embeddings; repeated n-gram filtering and loss masking
training.hardware: Jupiter: 1,024 H100 80GB (128 nodes, Austin, TX, Cirrascale); Augusta: 160 nodes of A3 Mega VMs, 8 H100 each (Google Cloud, Council Bluffs, Iowa); 7B mostly on Jupiter, 13B mostly on Augusta
training.compute: Training FLOPs approx 6 x tokens x params: OLMo 2 1B 0.4e23, 7B 1.8e23, 13B 4.6e23, 32B 13.0e23 (Tables 6, 22); total GPU power 131 MWh (7B), 257 MWh (13B)
training.seeds: Mid-training uses 3 or 4 different data orders (seeds) per model, then averages; post-training: 1 seed in sweeps, up to 4 for final hyperparameters

other.souping: 7B: average of 3 anneals x 50B; 13B and 32B: average of 4 (3 x 100B + 1 x 300B), found better than averaging the 3 x 100B alone
other.anneal_choice: 50B mix for 7B; 100B mix for 13B keeps the same number of LR-anneal steps given larger batch
other.post_training_SFT: effective batch 128, linear LR, warmup ratio 0.3; final LR 2e-5 (7B), 5e-6 (13B), 4e-6 (32B)
other.RM: LR 3e-6, effective batch 256, 1 epoch, max length 2048
other.RLVR_PPO: 7B: LR 4e-7, beta 0.05, batch 224, 100,000 episodes; 13B: LR 3e-7, beta 0.1/0.03/0.1 over three stages, batch 248, 200,000 episodes; gamma 1.0, lambda 0.95, clip 0.2, temperature 1.0, max length 2048, no-EOS penalty -10; value fn initialised from RM
other.RLVR_32B_1B: GRPO, no reward model; 32B LR 5e-7, KL beta 0.1, 16 samples per prompt

inference.temperature: 1.0 during RLVR generation; QwQ 32B eval used 0.6 with top-p 0.95, top-k 30
inference.prompting: OLMES: 5-shot curated in-context examples for most tasks; GSM8K 8-shot CoT; BBH 3-shot CoT; AGIEval 1-shot; MCF and CF formulations both run, best used (MMLU and held-out MC use MCF only)

metrics.name: Training FLOPs
metrics.definition: approx 6 x training tokens x model size (Kaplan et al., 2020)

metrics.name: Spike score

metrics.name: Growth exponent

eval.protocol: OLMES standard, dev tasks separated from held-out tasks; models were not evaluated on held-out sets before release; no seeds or significance tests reported for base comparisons

availability.code: OLMo, OLMo-core (pretraining), open-instruct (post-training), olmes (eval), dolma (data curation); Apache 2.0 where possible

prompts.text: Create a math problem related to the following persona: {persona} Note: 1. The math problem should be challenging and involve advanced mathematical skills and knowledge. Only top talents can solve it correctly. 2. You should make full use of the persona description to create the math problem to ensure that the math problem is unique and specific to the persona. 3. Your response should always start with "Math problem:". Your response should not include a solution to the created math problem. 4. Your created math problem should include no more than 2 sub-problems.

Provide solution to the given math problem. Problem: {generated_math_problem} Note: Provide your solution step-by-step, and end your solution in a new line in the following format: Final Answer: The final answer is $final_answer$. I hope it is correct.

limits: Pretraining energy, carbon and water reported only for 7B and 13B (not 32B or 1B); excludes embodied emissions, deployment, inference and development runs (authors call them lower bounds).
LR sweep limited by cost; the authors say a wider sweep is needed to bound the plateau, and the 2.8-point GSM8K edge for the higher LR is not dependable.
Spike and stability results come from short or reduced test settings (shortened warmup), judged by curves and a spike score, not repeated seeds.
n-gram to spike link is not deterministic (same sequence may spike for one model size or data order only).
OLMo 2 models were not evaluated on held-out sets before release; the authors cannot guarantee held-out sets are unseen by other models; GSM8K only partly held out (200 dev examples).
Qwen 2.5 token counts undisclosed, Mistral FLOPs unknowable, Qwen 3 and Zamba 2 FLOPs not reported, so the FLOPs comparison is approximate (6 x tokens x params).
1B model struggles; below some size the recipe may need task-specific data or distillation (hypothesis, not tested).
Instruct models were retrained after a tokenizer pre-tokenisation mismatch invalidated the preview release.
Inconsistent token and gain figures: 32B pretrain checkpoint is 7T tokens in Table 9 but 6.06T in Sec 2.3; mid-training gain text numbers differ from Table 9 means.

terms.definition: the shorter second stage (5-10% of FLOPs) where the LR is linearly decayed to zero on a smaller, higher-quality mix (Dolmino)
an annealing run on a small math or domain subset mixed about 50/50 with general data, used to assess one source cheaply
naive averaging of weights of checkpoints annealed on different data orders from the same pretraining checkpoint
percentage of values in a time series at least seven standard deviations from a rolling average of the last 1,000 values
lambda = (1/n_layers) log(||v'||/||v||), measure of activation or gradient expansion across layers
reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, e.g. PPO rewarded only when a math answer is correct
